title: Choosing a project team
intro: A software firm must choose a team of exactly four consultants from eight, A to H. Each has a daily fee (in thousands of rupees) and one or two of the three skills the project needs: web, data and security. The team's cost is the sum of its members' fees.
clues: At least one member has each of the three skills: web, data and security.
A and B never work on the same team.
C joins only if D also joins (D may join without C).
E and G never work on the same team.
F joins only if at least one of H and A also joins.

questions.stem: How many different teams satisfy all five conditions?
why: Split on A and B, who are never together: A without B gives 7 teams, B without A gives 5, and neither gives 1 (C, D, G, H).

questions.stem: What is the least possible cost of a valid team, in thousands of rupees?
why: The cheapest of the 13 teams are B, C, D, G (20 + 45 + 25 + 35) and B, D, E, H (20 + 25 + 40 + 40).
Both cost 125, and no valid team costs less.

questions.stem: Which pair of consultants is on every valid team of the least possible cost?
why: The two teams costing 125 are B, C, D, G and B, D, E, H.
Only B and D are on both.

questions.stem: Which consultant is on the largest number of valid teams?
why: Count appearances in the 13 teams: D 11, C 8, A 7, E 7, H 7, B 5, F 4, G 3.
D is on the most: every team with C needs D, and D is missing only from A, E, F, H and B, E, F, H.

questions.stem: The firm adds two more conditions: at most one of the three consultants with the security skill (A, B and G) may be on the team, and the team cost may not exceed 140. How many teams are now possible?
why: Drop the teams with two of A, B and G: A, C, D, G and B, C, D, G. 11 are left.
Drop those costing more than 140: A, C, D, E; A, C, D, H; A, E, F, H; C, D, G, H. 11 - 4 = 7.

steps: A and B are never together, so split into three cases: A without B, B without A, and neither. Condition 2 then needs no more checking.

A without B: A gives web and security, so a data person is needed. With C, D joins and the fourth is E, F, G or H (F is fine with A in): 4 teams. Without C, E joins, G is out, and two of D, F, H fill the team: 3 teams.
B without A: with C and D, the fourth is E, G or H (F needs H or A): 3 teams. Without C, E joins, G is out, and the pair from D, F, H must not leave F without H: B, D, E, H and B, E, F, H.
Neither A nor B: the only security person left is G, which keeps E out, so the data person is C, bringing D. The fourth is H (F has no A or H beside it): C, D, G, H.
Add up each team's fees for the cost questions.

diagram.note: One team a cell, by case; the last step adds each team's cost in thousands.
